decomposition.assessmentContext: These subjects are assessed by performance, portfolio or observation, not by a written exam split into parts. Leave the `aids` column empty and write no `aids.*` settings.
decomposition.courseSpecifics: The instructions for this family already tell the AI that it cannot hear or see a performance, and what to do instead. Do not repeat that in `slots.courseSpecifics`.
decomposition.loadBearingExamples: Load-bearing vocabulary is typically notation and technical terms whose everyday sense is vaguer or different: key, interval, beat, tempo, composition, perspective. Watch especially for everyday words the subject uses precisely, such as "higher" meaning pitch and not loudness; the everyday sense will otherwise be carried forward silently.
decomposition.nodeTypeCharacter: In these subjects much of what the student must master is practical: done with the voice, the body, an instrument or a material, and shown only by doing it. The AI cannot observe that performance and does not try to judge it, so the tree is a theory entry to the subject. Concept nodes hold the theory and terminology, and that is where the AI does its real teaching. Practical skills still earn nodes, because the map should show the whole subject and the student ticks them off after practising for real. A concept that needs extensive work on paper before it could be said to be practised (reading a rhythm, working out a key) is split into a concept node and a skill node exactly as in mathematics.
decomposition.prerequisiteDirection: The links that matter most run from theory to practice. Every practical skill node depends on the concept nodes that explain it, and those links are what gives the AI something to teach on that node. Within practice, beware false prerequisites: a beginner can sing, draw or improvise long before the technique is secure, so record a dependency only where one skill genuinely cannot be done without the other.
decomposition.selfAssessment: No one but the student and the teacher will judge a practical skill, so its description must name a result the student can check alone, preferably against a recording of themselves: "the short note lands on the right subdivision", not "sings dotted rhythms well". A description only a trained ear or eye could judge needs rewriting.
decomposition.skillVerbs: Two kinds. A skill carried out on notation or symbols is named as in mathematics: "Find the key from the key signature". A practical skill is named with the verb of the performance itself: "Sing an interval from a given note", "Draw a figure in proportion". Use the performance verb even though the AI will never see the performance; the node records what the student must be able to do, not what the AI can check.

add.text: Make tasks only on theory and notation. If a skill in the list is performed with the voice, the body, an instrument or a material, set no task on it, and say at the top of the test that those skills are assessed outside the chat, by doing them.

IN THIS SUBJECT the teacher can hear and see the students. For a goal performed with the voice, the body, an instrument or a material, the rounds are real practice: the teacher demonstrates, the students perform, and the teacher gives feedback on what they hear and see.
The automaticity argument in this subject: once reading the notation or the basic technique is automatic, your attention is free for the music, the picture or the movement itself.

If this skill is performed with the voice, the body, an instrument or a material, you cannot hear or see the performance. Say so, and never give feedback as if you had. Instead: explain the theory behind the skill, suggest concrete exercises the student can do alone, say what to listen or look for in a recording of themselves, go through the description above as a checklist they can assess themselves against, and ask how it went. On such a node the student decides when it is mastered, not you; this replaces `mastery` above.
